newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian crude - Sentiment bullish on Attaka rig fire.
newsitem.headline: Asian crude - Sentiment bullish on Attaka rig fire.

text.p: Sentiment on Asia's light crude market was bullish on Tuesday, on news of an October Tapis trade done at a high premium, and a cut in Indonesia's light sweet Attaka crude production following a rig fire, traders said.
A rig fire near Balikpapan had led to the temporary shutdown of the nearby Attaka and Santan crude fields.
By late Tuesday, the 73,000-barrel-per-day Attaka field had come back onstream, but was operating at half capacity, an official said.
Traders were unclear how much the shutdown would impact the spot market, as the extent of the loss in production was still to be ascertained, they said.
But it was expected to provide some support, since light crude availabilities was already tight in September.
The first October Tapis was sold by a producer at APPI +30 cents per barrel, higher than the last September Tapis deal done at APPI +18.
This gave further support to the market.
The buyer could not be confirmed, but was heard to be Japanese.
The heavy crude market was lacklustre, with deals done at steady levels.
China was heard to have bought 450,000 barrels of Cinta from an equity producer at ICP +20/25 cents, in line with the last Minas trade done at ICP +30.
Cinta usually trades just below Minas.
But the Middle East market remained active, with trades done at increasingly higher levels.
Oman was offered at MPM +10 for October, with bids at MPM +5.
This compares to the first October trades done at MPM +3, and MPM +5.
"The market has potential to go higher, although it will ultimately depend on how much China buys" said one western trader.
But other traders said that the lack of Yemeni Masila grade, Oman's competitor crude, in October, is likely to keep Oman prices up even without Chinese buying.
Yemen renews its crude term contracts every quarter, with Masila term customers expected to start negotiations for the fourth quarter contracts later this week.
But renewal of term contracts would usually be reached only after several week of talks, and term buyers would only offer spot cargoes after the term contracts are concluded.
The first Abu Dhabi Murban cargo for October was traded on Monday at ADNOC +14 to a shosha.
But subsequent trades were expected to be at firmer levels.
"It's very active today, and prices will definitely be higher," said a trader with a major oil company.
